reviewed_passages.credal:
The same calculation applies to an explicitly supplied **nonempty** joint
credal family containing the target law on the stated validity event, using
the infimum of complete-policy improvement over that family. An empty or
inconsistent family gives an invalid/conflict status, not a favorable infinite
improvement. A capped evaluator must certify a lower bound on the infimum;
evaluating one feasible law supplies an upper bound on it and is insufficient.
The family's acquisition, soundness and evaluation need their own evidence
contract. Independent marginal intervals generally discard useful
dependence; evaluating each branch against a different model can change the
decision problem. The existing [composition boundary](../foundations/01_composition_boundaries.md#cb05-a-tree-recursion-can-discard-shared-constraints)
already establishes that obstruction; this task imports it rather than
repeating that completed work.
reviewed_passages.offline_acquisition:
The tariff counts declared bounded primitive operations and 64-bit word
accesses. It is not elapsed CPU time, Python memory usage, or a claim that
all real-world administrative work has negligible cost. Source registration,
profile construction and numerical readout are explicitly priced. Raw audit
serialization and diagnostic snapshots are experiment instrumentation and
cannot be read by the deployed selector as a source of otherwise unpaid
information. The profile and audit requests are offline mathematical
evaluations: their hypothetical false-positive, false-negative and fallback
features describe deployment behavior, while the resources needed to obtain
them are paid. If acquiring observations itself incurs real task loss, that
loss must also enter setup or the complete episode's bill. Human theorem and
program development are research activities, not measured deployment operations
under this tariff.
